official.deadline_note: Two-stage process. Applicants must have a fully complete undergraduate application by the Early Action 2 deadline, published for the current cycle as January 3, 2027 (Early Action 1 was November 1, 2026). Eligible applicants are then invited to apply for the scholarship through the JWU Admissions Portal in January; the scholarship submission deadline itself is later and separate (JWU published February 6, 2026 for the 2026 cycle, when the EA2 application deadline was January 4, 2026). The 2027-cycle scholarship deadline has not yet been published.

official.english_requirement: JWU's published undergraduate admission requirement: IELTS 6.0 (subscores 5.5+), TOEFL iBT 75 (subscores 15+), Duolingo English Test 105 (subscore 90), PTE Academic 53 (subscore 43+), or TOEFL Essentials 8; results must be no more than two years old and submitted on an official transcript or report form. Applicants from majority English-speaking countries (e.g., UK, Canada except Quebec, Australia, Ireland, Nigeria, Ghana) may be exempt based on transcript review.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an invitation-only route, not a direct application: a non-U.S. citizen must first file a complete undergraduate application to JWU by the Early Action 2 deadline (3 January 2027 for Fall 2027 entry) and only then receive a portal invitation to compete. The prize is full tuition, $45,408 a year at 2026-27 published rates, but nothing toward housing, meals, fees or insurance, so a Providence winner still faces roughly $19,600 of other first-year direct costs. Draft the Global Impact Statement and line up two recommenders before the January invitation arrives, because the scholarship window is short and separate from the admission deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-U.S. citizen high-school leavers with strong transcripts and a documented record of leadership in extracurricular, volunteer or entrepreneurial activity who can commit to an Early Action application to the Providence or Charlotte campus.
application_readiness_checklist: Complete the JWU application (or Common App) listing every school attended, with secondary transcripts showing subjects, marks and graduation date, plus certified translations if they are not in English

Sit an accepted English test early enough that results are under two years old at application (IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 75 / Duolingo 105 / PTE 53 undergraduate minimums); send TOEFL scores under JWU's DI code 3465
Draft the Global Impact Statement and brief two recommenders before the January invitation window opens

Prepare the financial declaration form and bank or sponsor documents early; a scholarship award can be subtracted from the proof-of-funds figures ($73,500 Providence / $70,000 Charlotte for one academic year)
Monitor the JWU Admissions Portal and email in January for the scholarship invitation, since nothing can be submitted without it
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete undergraduate application by the Early Action 2 deadline: the eligibility gate requires a fully complete application, so missing transcripts or documents end the bid before the scholarship stage
Assuming a direct scholarship application exists and waiting for one that never arrives, missing the portal invitation window
A generic Global Impact Statement with no concrete evidence of extracurricular, volunteer or entrepreneurial leadership
Applying as a graduate, transfer, online or domestic student, or to a campus other than Providence or Charlotte
English test scores older than two years, which can hold up admission and therefore scholarship consideration
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition only. At JWU's published 2026-27 rates a Providence first-year student should still budget about $19,586 in other direct costs (housing $11,500, gold meal plan $7,360, new student fee $476, activity fee $250) plus the $1,386 international student service fee and $2,670 health insurance plan if not otherwise covered; Charlotte's equivalents are about $13,260. ESL coursework, where required, adds $5,250 per semester, and books, supplies and travel are not covered.
document_audit: Unofficial transcripts are enough to apply, but official documents must be submitted before enrolling in classes
Transcripts not in English require a certified translation; all schools attended must be listed with dates
English proficiency reports must be on an official transcript or report form no more than two years old
Bank statements for the I-20 must be issued within the last three months and can be in a parent's, family member's or sponsor's name
The Global Impact Statement and two letters of recommendation are scholarship-stage documents uploaded through the JWU Admissions Portal, separate from the admission file
alerts: The award disappeared from JWU's redesigned live scholarship listing in October 2026 even though JWU's international admissions page still promotes it; confirm with JWU Admissions that the 2027-cycle round is running before relying on it
The scholarship deadline is separate from and later than the application deadline (February 6, 2026 in the last cycle versus January 4, 2026 for EA2), so both dates must be diarised separately
Only Providence and Charlotte campus students qualify; JWU Online students are ineligible for JWU institutional scholarships
Early Action is non-binding, so applying by 3 January 2027 costs nothing (there is no application fee) and keeps the scholarship route open without committing to enrol
Even with full tuition, the I-20 financial proof still requires showing living-cost funds, so family savings or a sponsor remain necessary
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the admission application by Early Action 2 (3 January 2027); eligible applicants are invited through the JWU Admissions Portal in January and upload the Global Impact Statement and two letters of recommendation there by the scholarship deadline; a JWU faculty and staff committee then decides from the transcripts, the statement and the letters.
